---
title: Write in a working copy
description: Keep part of an instance on your machine with marfa device, read and write it with no connection, and send the writes when you can.
---

`marfa device` keeps a [working copy](/build/devices) of part of an instance in one file. Reads come from the copy, and each write waits in a queue until you send it. Use it for a script or an agent that must keep working offline. An app built on the [Swift SDK](/swift-sdk) keeps the same kind of copy.

Every `marfa device` command names the file with `--db`, or with `MARFA_DB` for a whole shell. The commands that reach the server, `hydrate`, `catch-up`, `follow` and `drain`, use the CLI's server and key, as [Connect to a server](/cli#connect-to-a-server) shows. Reads and queued writes need only the file.

## Fill the copy

Choose the types and the [tier](/build/items-and-types) to keep, then fill the copy. Repeat `--type` for each type; the types beneath each come too:

<Terminal>

```bash
export MARFA_DB=./copy.sqlite
marfa device hydrate --type core.media --type core.file --tier library
```

```text
hydrated 6 item(s) and 1 edge(s) of core.media,core.file at library in 2 page(s); cursor 20
```

</Terminal>

`--type '*'` keeps every type except `system.*`, and `--tier all` keeps the library and the feed. `--edge-type` keeps every edge of a type the key reads; repeat it for more. A hydration that stops part way carries on from where it stopped when you run it again.

`marfa device status` says how the copy stands:

- **Whether it's whole:** the hydration is `never`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `stale` or `expired`.
- **When it last synced:** `synced_at` is when the copy last finished a pull from the server, by this machine's clock. An app can show it as "Updated 5 minutes ago".
- **Its files:** the file budget and the attached files the copy holds, as [Keep files on a device](/build/keep-files-on-a-device) explains.

## Read from the copy

`marfa device items get`, `items list` and `search` answer as the server does, from the copy. Under `--json`, a list prints `data` and `next_cursor` as the server's lists do, and adds `completeness`: `complete`, `partial` while the copy fills, or `stale` when it's behind the server.

```bash
marfa device items list --type core.media.book --sort updated-at --direction desc
marfa device search "Warden"
```

**Every item carries `read_only`**, the server's advice that a connector keeps the item and an app shouldn't offer to edit it. The copy holds the value the server last gave and refreshes it at most every 15 minutes, so it can be that far behind. It's advice only: the copy and the server both take a write to a read-only item. An item that hasn't reached the server yet reads `false`.

**The copy keeps the items in its slice that go to the bin.** `--state trashed` lists them with no connection, and `--state any` lists every state. `marfa device items bin` reads the instance's whole bin instead; it needs the server and keeps nothing.

### Read while another process writes

One process at a time writes a copy. A second process, such as a menu bar helper beside an app, opens the same file with `--reader`. **A reading handle writes nothing**, not even housekeeping, and a write through it is refused `reading_handle`. Where no copy exists yet, `--reader` is refused `no_store` instead of making one.

## Write to the copy

A write shows in the copy at once and waits in the queue:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device items create --type core.media.book \
  --properties '{"title": "North and South", "author": "Elizabeth Gaskell"}'
```

```text
queued create_item 01a1f125-00cb-7296-929b-adf702216fa1 as 01a1f125-00cd-71d9-813e-3aae02856efa
```

</Terminal>

The first ID is the item's, the second the queued write's. A create is one write: `--state`, the capture location (`--capture-latitude` and `--capture-longitude`) and `--edges` go in its body, and each `--tag` follows as a write of its own. If the instance refuses any edge in it, it creates neither the item nor the edges.

An update names the version it was based on, as it does at the server. **An item created here is at version `0` until the server answers its create.**

```bash
marfa device items update <id> --version 1 --properties '{"progress": "started"}'
marfa device items trash <id>
marfa device items restore <id>
```

`--clear-property <name>` removes one property, and `--replace` makes `--properties` the whole set. `--occurred-at` sets the item's own time, and `--clear-occurred-at` removes it. Edges have commands of their own: [Write edges in a working copy](/build/edges-in-a-working-copy).

**The copy refuses at once a write the instance would refuse as malformed,** with the instance's code, and queues nothing. A write larger than the instance's request limit, which the copy reads at each drain, is refused with the device's own code, `over_request_limit`, and the write's size and the limit in bytes ([request limit rules](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md#a-body-over-the-servers-request-limit)).

## Send the queue

`marfa device drain` sends the queued writes in order and records each answer. A write that meets a network error stays for the next drain.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device drain
```

```text
marfa: writing to http://localhost:8600
merged update_item 01a1f122-697a-7360-a04e-48120ed3a8b5 merged title
the server answered 1 write(s)
```

</Terminal>

`marfa device queue` lists every write, its body and its [verdict](/build/devices#verdicts). `accepted` and `merged` need nothing; a merge is the server combining your change with a newer one, by the type's rules. Act on the three that need you:

| Verdict | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `refused` | Read the body, fix it in a new write, then take the refused one out with `marfa device discard <id>`. |
| `blocked` | Do what its reason needs, as [Verdicts](/build/devices#verdicts) lists. `marfa device release <id>` sends it again, and `marfa device withdraw <id>` takes it out and puts the copy back to what the instance holds. |
| `dead` | `marfa device release <id>` sends it again. |

`marfa device forget` clears the writes the instance has answered, which keeps later writes fast. It keeps each refused write that carried content until you discard it.

## Keep it current

`marfa device catch-up` applies what changed on the instance since the last hydration or catch-up, and `marfa device follow` holds the event stream open and applies each change as it comes. Add `--for-seconds` to stop following after a while.

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device catch-up --json
```

```json
{
  "applied": 0,
  "skipped": 0,
  "read_only_held": 0,
  "cursor": "8",
  "catalog_changed": false,
  "tables": {
    "whole": 0,
    "online": 0,
    "unfilled": 0,
    "pages": 0,
    "rows": 0,
    "failed": 0,
    "failure": null
  },
  "changed_tables": []
}
```

</Terminal>

**`applied` counts events; `read_only_held` counts items whose `read_only` the refresh changed.** No event brings a `read_only` change, so the two are kept apart. `read_only_held` is in the JSON only: the plain output adds `N item(s) took a new read_only` when it isn't zero.

A copy away longer than the instance keeps events becomes `stale`. One whose instance or reach changed expires, and so does a copy after a drain that moved an edge's from item: hydrate it again, and the writes not yet sent stay. Every read that goes to the server first checks it's the instance the copy was built from, and ends `copy_expired` if another answers. [Fix a working copy that can't catch up](/build/fix-a-working-copy) says what to run for each.

The rules behind this guide are in the [device](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/device.md) and [queue and verdicts](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md) chapters of the contract.
